Open source architecture for iot based SCADA system for smart home
authors: SD Grigorescu, GC Seritan, BA Enache, FC Argatu, FC Adochiei
venue: The Scientific Bulletin of Electrical Engineering Faculty 20 (1), 33-36, 2020

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The Internet of Things is considered an emerging technology with the potential to penetrate all aspects of our lives. However, with great power comes great responsibility and the privacy and security needed for critical infrastructure or sensitive commercial operations is very different than the needs of a Smart Home. Additionally, the available security resources from the private sector are totally different than the ones available to a homeowner. In this context, we developed an open source architecture for IoT which is based on the advantages of a SCADA system and can be easily applied to a Smart Home. This architecture assures a high-security level, even for low technical skills homeowners, with minimal costs.</jats:p>
title: Open Source Architecture for Iot Based SCADA System for Smart Home

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The development of intelligent smart grids requires new electrical monitoring solutions in order to optimize power consumption. The implementation of intelligent energy-monitors leads to new technical developments to optimize consumption using intrusive and non-intrusive techniques. This paper makes a review of the main methods used for load monitoring systems, indicating their advantages and disadvantages. The emergence of high-harmonic consumer electronics in electrical networks such as LED lighting sources implies the choice of the appropriate method and equipment for optimizing energy consumption based on energy signatures.</jats:p>
title: Load Monitoring Solutions for the Smart Buildings – An Overview

abstract: <jats:p>Accurate estimation of the State of Health (SoH) of lithium-ion batteries is a key requirement for ensuring the reliability, safety, and longevity of modern energy storage systems (ESS). As large numbers of cells reach the end of their initial service life, repurposing them for second-life applications such as stationary and renewable energy storage introduces new diagnostic challenges. In these cases, the original manufacturing data and degradation history are often unknown, making conventional model-based or laboratory-based SoH evaluation impractical. Traditional approaches based on equivalent circuit or electrochemical models offer physical interpretability but are computationally intensive and highly sensitive to parameter uncertainty. Data-driven techniques, particularly those employing machine learning (ML), have emerged as flexible alternatives capable of capturing the nonlinear relationships between measurable electrical signals and degradation states. Among them, artificial neural networks (ANNs) achieve a favorable compromise between predictive accuracy and computational efficiency. This paper presents the design, implementation, and validation of a lightweight ANN-based method for SoH estimation of second-life Li-ion cells using partial discharge voltage data. The model architecture, optimized for embedded deployment, balances accuracy with memory and processing efficiency. Experimental validation demonstrates that the proposed ANN achieves robust SoH prediction performance while remaining compatible with resource-constrained Tiny Machine Learning (TinyML) platforms. The results confirm that accurate and scalable battery health assessment can be achieved through compact neural architectures operating directly at the edge, offering a practical solution for distributed, autonomous, and sustainable energy storage management.</jats:p>
title: A TinyML-Driven Edge Computing Framework for State of Health Estimation of Second-Life Li-Ion Battery
